definition: The science of doing the most good. It studies charity as a system: where generosity flows, why it flows there, and how to route it from the symptoms of problems to their sources.
Someone who practices charitology: studying, testing, teaching or improving how generosity is aimed. Anyone can be one. The field is open.
A problem as it shows up in people’s lives: hunger tonight, an untreated illness, a flooded home. Symptoms are real and urgent, and most of them keep coming back until their sources change.

Something upstream that keeps producing problems, often many at once. Humanity’s Checklist names six: the story we tell, how we coordinate, what we can picture, what our feeds reward, what we admire and who gets to build.

Where on the chain from symptom to source a piece of work acts, on a five-level scale: relief, repair, prevention, structure, source. Every level is needed. Depth describes the work. It does not grade it.
What would have happened without a gift or program. The real effect of giving is the difference between the world with it and the world without it.
The share of an outcome that would not have happened without a particular gift. A gift to work that would have been funded anyway has low additionality.
How few resources already go to a problem relative to its size. Other things equal, an extra dollar does more where few dollars go.
